as_told.title: Remote viewing of a giant Soviet submarine (TK-089) inside a building, confirmed 114 days later
as_told.place_text: Soviet harbor north of the Arctic Circle

plain: In 1979, the story goes, a soldier named Joe McMoneagle was asked to describe a sealed building at a Russian shipyard on the White Sea using remote viewing alone. Remote viewing is a practice, once studied by the US government, of trying to see distant places with the mind. He described a huge new nuclear submarine being built inside. Michels tells it twice, once with the 1979 date and once from his own interview with McMoneagle, where he puts it in "78 or 79" and does not name the shipyard. McMoneagle tells it himself: "what I got was a really unique submarine." In his version the site is north of the Arctic Circle, the submarine is called TK-089, his report went to the National Security Council and to Robert Gates, a senior intelligence official, and the submarine was confirmed 114 days later. If it is true, it would mean the mind can gather real intelligence across great distances.
